questions.explain: A `static` local variable is initialised once and keeps its value between calls, so the counter goes 1, 2, 3.
option_notes: That would be an ordinary local variable (re-initialised on every call), but here it is static.
Correct: the static variable survives between calls.
It starts at 0 but is incremented before it is returned (`++n`).
Nothing makes the three calls return the same value.

options: It is an unsigned integer type
It is the type of the result of `sizeof`
It can hold the size of the largest object the system can address
questions.explain: `size_t` is an unsigned type chosen by the implementation to hold object sizes. On a 64-bit system it is typically 8 bytes, so it is not always 4. Print it with `%zu`.
option_notes: False: it is typically 8 bytes on 64-bit systems.
